# Stale Proof — TrustDecay

> Paste the history of any check (CI runs, audits, re-verifications) and get how much it should be trusted
> today, plus the exact date it must be re-run. Evidence fades to unknown, not to green. Runs entirely in the
> browser; nothing is sent anywhere.

## How it works
- One run is not proof: a single fresh pass scores 75% with the default prior, below the 80% bar.
- Silence fades to unknown: each pass/fail weighs 2^(-age/halfLife); with no new runs the score drifts back to
  the prior (50%), never to 0% and never to 100%.
- Recent beats old: a failure yesterday costs more than the same failure last quarter.
- The re-verify date is closed-form: reverifyBy = the earlier of staleAt and lapseAt.
- Verdicts: TRUSTED, DOUBTED (below the bar, re-run now), STALE (not enough live evidence, re-run now).

## Proof of play
- 37 tests including a 10,648-case garbage fuzz with zero throws; witness mutation gate CLEAN 61/61, nothing
  baselined. The live page imports the exact kernel.mjs the gate tests.

## Credit
- Letting evidence fade back to unknown rather than staying green (an old pass held steady can still be wrong),
  and STALE as a verdict that says "not enough live evidence, re-run" instead of guessing, draw on the Guided
  Entropy Principle (GEP) result that a stable system can stabilize a wrong reference, and on "I don't know"
  (PENDING) as an allowed verdict: Gary W. Floyd, Lumiea Systems Research Division — ThunderStruck Service LLC — "From GEP Stabilization to Dual-Map Ethical Reasoning: A derivation of positive ethical evidence, negative ethical evidence, and non-legal moral reasoning," Derivation v0.2. Open Defensive Prior Art (Creative Commons).
- Stale Proof itself is the estate's own work, authored by Kar for AI-Native Solutions. Powered by
  the Konomi architecture, created by Thomas Frumkin. MIT.
